chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: All-night playing with Sal Salvador, Tal Farlow and Jimmy Raney
summary: Four guitarists met nightly in New York for a year to play and talk, with Arv Garrison dropping in, while Collins stayed in town between Slam and Tadd Dameron.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, he married Kay. Yes, that's right. Frank Rosolino. That was a very good band, also. And I think the guitarists have a Sal Salvador. I'm sure it was. Now Sal, I met Sal in New York. He came down to study with Harry Volpe, and we did -- we hung out quite a bit together. Sal Salvador -- Tal Farlow, Jimmie Raney and myself had a thing; every night we met and we played all night long. This was every night. I would leave home about 12:00 o'clock and I would get home the next day about 9:00 or 10:00. And what would happen, we'd have coffee and we just would play all night long, talk, play, draw, you know, just -- but music was the thing that was -- Sal, Jimmie Raney, and Tal Farlow and myself, in New York. None of us had any money. Great expectations, you know.

But some good things came out of that. Jimmie Raney was a tremendous guitarist also. I admired him very much. Tal Farlow was -- whew, he was something else, also. But it was kind of like a mutual admiration society.
Yeah, this is all we would do all night long, just play. And this went on for -- geez, a year.

And one guy would come up occasionally, Arv Garrison. I don't know whether you ever heard of him, but it was a Vivien Garry Trio of -- he was a tremendous guitarist from Toledo, I think. I think he was an epileptic or something, and he died. But he was a tremendous guitarist, he did some very nice things, real quick, you know, and then he went back to Toledo because he had this epilepsy. And I think he died. But he would come up occasionally, and this was a very important time in my life because I got a chance again to do some things that I wanted to do with guitars, you know.

When was this. This was around -- in the late forties and early fifties, I think. Yeah, I'm sure it was around that time, yeah. It was around that time. And in the interim I was working around between Slam and Tad Dameron, and doing some things. But the main thing, the important thing was I was staying in New York rather than travelling. And that was good, well that's good for any musician because New York is a very invigorating city. It's electric, it's a feeling that no other city has. You've got to want to -- just being there makes you want to study and to do things, you know.
